ur5e_dt.play_scene.description: Start/resume the simulation timeline. Restores the saved twin's Python ROS callbacks; Newton twin playback uses CPU and needs a stopped stage before first initialization. Does not rebuild saved graphs or switch physics engines.

ur5e_dt.stop_scene.description: Stop the UR5e twin's simulation timeline, e.g. before generic sim__* edits. Stop rewinds physics to the authored start pose. For other scenes use sim__timeline__control.

ur5e_dt.setup_camera_tf_graph.description: Import the RealSense camera, attach it to the UR5e wrist and build its ROS 2 action graph (camera image, camera_info and the /tf_cam transform tree). Requires the UR5e to be loaded (e.g. after quick_start_with_workstation).

ur5e_dt.assemble_objects.description: Uses your own lab files from the asset folder, which cannot be downloaded (see docs/ASSETS.md). Assemble objects into a specified configuration.

assembly.description: Assembly configuration; fmb4 is Jenga, also accepted as jenga or fmb_jenga

fields.name: assembly
fields.description: Assembly configuration; fmb4 is Jenga, also accepted as jenga or fmb_jenga

ur5e_dt.randomize_object_poses.description: Randomize the positions of non-base objects in /World/Objects of the UR5e twin, after ur5e_dt__add_objects.

ur5e_dt.randomize_single_object.description: Randomize the position of a single named object in a clear workspace area, keeping all other objects fixed.

object_name.description: Name of the object to randomize (e.g. 'inverted_u_yellow')

fields.name: object_name
fields.description: Name of the object to randomize (e.g. 'inverted_u_yellow')

ur5e_dt.save_scene_state.description: Save the UR5e twin's object poses to a JSON file in its scene_states folder, for ur5e_dt__restore_scene_state. A file of that name is replaced; with no name it gets a timestamp. Returns result, file_path and, on failure, error.

json_file_path.description: Path to save file. If omitted, a timestamped filename is used.

fields.name: json_file_path
fields.description: Path to save file. If omitted, a timestamped filename is used.

ur5e_dt.restore_scene_state.description: Restore the UR5e twin's object poses from a JSON file made by ur5e_dt__save_scene_state. Returns result and, on failure, error.

json_file_path.description: Path to restore from. If omitted, the most recent save is used.

fields.name: json_file_path
fields.description: Path to restore from. If omitted, the most recent save is used.

ur5e_dt.add_objects.description: Uses your own lab files from the asset folder, which cannot be downloaded (see docs/ASSETS.md). Add objects to the scene from a predefined assembly folder.

assembly.description: Assembly folder; fmb4 is Jenga, also accepted as jenga or fmb_jenga

fields.name: assembly
fields.description: Assembly folder; fmb4 is Jenga, also accepted as jenga or fmb_jenga

ur5e_dt.delete_objects.description: Delete all objects from /World/Objects of the UR5e twin and the associated pose publisher graph.

ur5e_dt.setup_pose_publisher.description: Create an action graph publishing the UR5e twin's object poses to ROS 2 topic objects_poses_sim, after ur5e_dt__add_objects.

ur5e_dt.start_ros_driver.description: Bring the ROS 2 driver of the lab's UR5e twin up, down or report status, so robot-motion tools have a driver. backend='fake' (default) is sim only, with mock hardware and no Docker, ready in seconds; 'ursim' needs Docker and is the path to mode='real' (not yet enabled). Refuses if another UR driver is detected. Stop the fake driver before stopping its simulator. Managed sim__launch sessions support only fake. Use once at startup.

mode.description: 'sim' (default) or 'real' (lab UR5e — not yet enabled; requires backend='ursim').

action.description: 'up' (default) brings the driver up, 'down' tears it down, 'status' reports state.

backend.description: 'fake' (default) = apt ur_robot_driver fake hardware via launch_ur_fake.sh (lightweight, sim only); 'ursim' = URSim docker via sim_bringup.sh (needs Docker + ~/ros2_ws; required for mode='real'; unavailable in managed sessions).

fields.name: mode

ur5e_dt.sync_real_poses.description: Wait up to 3 seconds for /objects_poses_real and update matching sim objects. Reports an error if no message or matching objects arrive, and lists updated and snapped objects.

ur5e_dt.new_stage.description: Clear the entire USD stage and free accumulated memory. Use this when Isaac Sim's process memory has grown large after many scene loads/resets. This tears down all USD prims, Hydra render state, and PhysX allocations. The scene will be empty afterwards — use quick_start to rebuild it.

ur5e_dt.quick_start.description: RISE lab UR5e digital twin; for a generic start, see sim__quick_start. One-click scene setup from public assets: loads the scene, imports NVIDIA's UR5e with action graphs, creates a workspace camera and starts simulation. Adds the RG2 gripper only when its files are in the asset folder; the result's gripper field says which happened. Uses CPU physics in the selected engine; an existing non-CPU World is refused. Use after new_stage to rebuild a disposable scene.

ur5e_dt.start_recording.description: Start real-time viewport video recording using ffmpeg. Records frames from the viewport render buffer without blocking physics. Returns immediately — call stop_recording to finalize the video.

file_name.description: Output filename (e.g. 'my_recording.mp4'). Saved to the configured VIDEOS_DIR. Defaults to 'realtime_recording.mp4'.

camera.description: Camera prim path to record from (e.g. '/World/workspace_camera_sim'). If omitted, uses the active viewport camera.

fps.description: Frames per second for the output video. Defaults to 30.

fields.name: file_name
fields.description: Output filename (e.g. 'my_recording.mp4'). Saved to the configured VIDEOS_DIR. Defaults to 'realtime_recording.mp4'.

ur5e_dt.stop_recording.description: Stop the current real-time viewport recording and finalize the MP4 video file. Returns the output file path and frame count.

ur5e_dt.get_recording_status.description: Check if viewport video recording is currently active. Returns status, frame count, elapsed time, output path, and FPS.

ur5e_dt.load_workstation.description: Load the Vention bench as visual context under the lab's UR5e twin, at /World/Vention with its top at z=0. Uses your own lab file from the asset folder, which cannot be downloaded (see docs/ASSETS.md); a placeholder bench is used without it. Additive (cleared by new_stage), visual-only and safe while playing. Does not move the robot.

ur5e_dt.quick_start_with_workstation.description: RISE lab UR5e digital twin. Uses your own lab files from the asset folder, which cannot be downloaded (see docs/ASSETS.md). A placeholder bench is used without them. Same as quick_start, then loads the Vention workstation bench (see load_workstation). One call builds the full robot+scene and drops the bench underneath. quick_start itself is unchanged.

ur5e_dt.load_simple_room.description: Load Isaac's standard Simple Room environment (floor, walls, window, lamp) as a backdrop. Additive (cleared by new_stage): references the standard Isaac Simple_Room asset onto /World/SimpleRoom at z=-0.11 so it matches the source scene under the robot-base-at-0 convention (the Vention bench feet land on the room floor). Hides the default ground plane visual while keeping its z=0 collider, so object/robot physics are unchanged. Does not move the robot. Best used together with load_workstation.

ur5e_dt.quick_start_with_workstation_and.description: RISE lab UR5e digital twin. Uses your own lab files from the asset folder, which cannot be downloaded (see docs/ASSETS.md). A placeholder bench is used without them. Same as quick_start, then loads the Vention workstation bench AND the Simple Room backdrop. One call builds the full robot+scene, the bench under the robot, and the room around it. quick_start itself is unchanged.

ur5e_dt.set_object_pose.description: Teleport a scene object under /World/Objects to an EXACT world pose. Use to set up controlled scenes — e.g. placing two parts close together to exercise neighbour-aware grasp gating. Applies via the same xformOp path randomize uses, so it persists under physics (object stays put on play). Mirror it with setup_pose_publisher so /objects_poses_sim reflects the new pose.

position.description: [x, y, z] world position in METERS.

orientation.description: Optional [w, x, y, z] quaternion. If given, overrides yaw_deg.

yaw_deg.description: Optional yaw rotation about world z in degrees (used when orientation is omitted). Default 0 (identity).
